note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a JAM 6, Schedule 2-3; A06b JAM 6, Schedule 2-3; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: No provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Generally applicable provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory unconditionally; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad (the dataset codes no separate descent rule for a child born in the country, birth there giving it; the parent's sex is read from mode A01b). Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Jamaica, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Jamaica for 12 months immediately prior to the application, as well as for 4 out of 7 years predating the 12-month period. Intent to reside in Jamaica required. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... No provision ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a Jamaican mother, or to a non-Jamaican mother married to a Jamaican citizen, residing abroad in the employment of the Jamaican diplomatic service. Person is born to a citizen iure soli, iure sanguinis or by registration due to marriage to a citizen.; Person is a minor and born abroad to a citizen not covered by Article 3C Constitution (see above). ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Jamaica. Unless born to a foreign diplomat and neither parent is a citizen, or one of the parents is an enemy alien and child is born in a place then under occupation by the enemy. Person is deemed to be born in the country if at the time of birth the mother is a citizen residing abroad in the diplomatic service of Jamaica, or if -regardless whether she is a citizen- the mother resides abroad as the spouse of a citizen who works in the diplomatic service of Jamaica. ... No provision
